```text
{"body":"### Is your proposal related to a problem?\n\nEvent types can already force a **cancellation** reason. The `CancellationReasonRequirement` enum (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`) offers `MANDATORY_BOTH` / `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` / `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` / `OPTIONAL_BOTH`, it is stored on `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:287`), and it is enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`.\n\nRescheduling has no equivalent. A `rescheduleReason` is collected (`packages/lib/bookings/SystemField.ts:10`, `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`) but it is always optional — `rg -n \"requiresRescheduleReason|RescheduleReasonRequirement\"` over the repo returns nothing.\n\nSo a host who needs accountability gets it for cancellations and silently loses it for reschedules, even though a reschedule disrupts the same attendee and moves the same calendar. Hosts who run paid or high-demand event types are the ones who feel it.\n\n### Describe the solution you'd like\n\nMirror the cancellation setting for reschedules:\n\n- a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum and a `requiresRescheduleReason` column on `EventType`, with the same four values and the same default posture;\n- a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced, sitting next to the cancellation one;\n- validation on the reschedule path that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`;\n- the reason surfaced wherever the cancellation reason already is.\n\n### User story\n\nAs a host, I want to require a reason when someone reschedules one of my bookings, so that I have the same record of why my calendar moved that I already have for cancellations.\n\n### Rough scope\n\n**Medium.** The whole pattern already exists end to end — enum, column, migration (`packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/`), settings dropdown, validation, and unit tests in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/test/handleCancelBooking.test.ts` — so this is one migration plus a parallel copy of known-good code, not a new design.\n\n### Source\n\n`specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/future-work.md`, which lists \"Reschedule reason requirement (same pattern, separate setting)\" as work deliberately deferred from that feature.\n\n### Additional context\n\nIntended labels: `type: feature`, `scope: medium`. Nearest existing labels: `enhancement`, `effort:medium`. 1	import { CancellationReasonRequirement } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
```
```text
2	
```
```text
3	export function isCancellationReasonRequired(
4	  setting: CancellationReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
5	  isHost: boolean
6	): boolean {
7	  const requirement = setting ?? CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;
8	
9	  switch (requirement) {
10	    case CancellationReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
11	      return false;
12	    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
13	      return true;
14	    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
15	      return isHost;
16	    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
17	      return !isHost;
18	    default:
19	      return false;
20	  }
21	}
22
```

 `./specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/design.md`

```text
1	# Cancellation Reason Requirement Design
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Add a dropdown setting in Event Type Advanced settings that allows hosts to configure when cancellation reasons are required from hosts and/or attendees.
6	
7	## Problem Statement
8	
9	Currently, cancellation reasons are always optional. Hosts need the ability to require reasons for better tracking and accountability.
10	
11	## User Stories
12	
13	- As a host, I want to require cancellation reasons from attendees so that I understand why bookings are cancelled
14	- As a host, I want to require my team to provide cancellation reasons so that we have records of why bookings were cancelled
15	- As a host, I want to make cancellation reasons optional when they're not needed
16	
17	## Technical Design
18	
19	### Database Changes
20	
21	Add new enum `CancellationReasonRequirement` with values:
22	- `MANDATORY_BOTH`
23	- `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`
24	- `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY`
25	- `OPTIONAL_BOTH`
26	
27	Add column `requiresCancellationReason` to EventType model with default `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`.
28	
29	Location: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` (near `disableCancelling`/`disableRescheduling`)
30	
31	### API Changes
32	
33	Update `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` to validate cancellation reason based on:
34	- Event type's `requiresCancellationReason` setting
35	- Who is cancelling (host vs attendee)
36	
37	### UI Changes
38	
39	**Event Type Settings**
40	
41	Location: `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx`
42	
43	Add dropdown after Booking Questions section, before RequiresConfirmationController:
44	- Label: "Require cancellation reason"
45	- Description: "Ask for a reason when someone cancels a booking"
46	- Options: Mandatory for both, Mandatory for host only (default), Mandatory for attendee only, Optional for both
47	
48	**Cancel Booking**
49	
50	Location: `apps/web/components/booking/CancelBooking.tsx`
51	
52	- Add `requiresCancellationReason` prop
53	- Replace hardcoded `hostMissingCancellationReason` logic with configurable validation based on the setting
54	- Show required indicator on textarea when reason is required
55	
56	## Data Flow
57	
58	1. EventType stores `requiresCancellationReason` in database
59	2. `getEventTypesFromDB` (`apps/web/lib/booking.ts`) includes the field in select
60	3. Value flows through page props to booking views
61	4. `CancelBooking` component uses it for validation
62	
63	Files requiring prop threading:
64	- `apps/web/lib/booking.ts`
65	- `apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.tsx`
66	- `apps/web/components/dialog/CancelBookingDialog.tsx`
67	
68	## Edge Cases
69	
70	- Platform users: Should respect the setting
71	- Team bookings: Setting applies regardless of team context
72	- Null column value: Default to `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` behavior
73	- Default event types (no eventTypeId): Use default `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`
74	
75	## Out of Scope
76	
77	- Reschedule reason configuration (separate feature)
78	- Custom reason dropdown options
79	- Reason analytics/reporting
80
```

```text
136	    if (!eventTypeMetadata?.apps || !appId) return null;
137	    const apps = eventTypeMetadata.apps as Record<string, unknown>;
138	    return (apps[appId] as Record<string, unknown>) || null;
139	  };

146	    : null;

149	    if (props.isHost) return false; // Hosts/organizers are exempt

151	    if (!booking?.startTime) return false;

153	    if (!booking?.payment) return false;
```

```text
31	function preprocessField({

33	  value,
34	  isPartialSchema,
35	  log,

44	  if (fieldTypeSchema) {

47	      isPartialSchema,
48	      field,
49	    });
50	  }
51	  if (field.type === "boolean") {
52	    // Turn a boolean in string to a real boolean
53	    return value === "true" || value === true;
54	  }
55	  // Make sure that the value is an array

63	      value: "",

65	    try {
66	      parsedValue = JSON.parse(value);
67	    } catch (e) {
68	      log.error(`Failed to parse JSON for field ${field.name}`, e);
69	    }
70	    const optionsInputs = field.optionsInputs;
71	    const optionInputField = optionsInputs?.[parsedValue.value];
72	    if (optionInputField && optionInputField.type === "phone") {
73	      parsedValue.optionValue = ensureValidPhoneNumber(parsedValue.optionValue);
74	    }
75	    return parsedValue;
76	  } else if (field.type === "phone") {
77	    return ensureValidPhoneNumber(typeof value === "string" ? value : String(value));
78	  } else {
79	    return value;
80	  }

293	/**
294	 * Checks if a booker email matches an email/domain entry.
295	 * Supports three formats:
296	 * - Full email: "user@example.com" - matches exactly
297	 * - Domain with @ prefix: "@example.com" - matches any email ending with "@example.com"
298	 * - Domain without @ prefix: "example.com" - matches any email ending with "@example.com"
299	 */
300	const doesEmailMatchEntry = (bookerEmail: string, entry: string): boolean => {
301	  const bookerEmailLower = bookerEmail.toLowerCase();
302	
303	  if (entry.startsWith("@")) {
304	    const domain = entry.slice(1).toLowerCase();
305	    return bookerEmailLower.endsWith("@" + domain);
306	  }
307	
308	  if (entry.includes("@")) {
309	    return bookerEmailLower === entry.toLowerCase();
310	  }
311	
312	  return bookerEmailLower.endsWith("@" + entry.toLowerCase());
313	};
314	export const getBookingResponsesPartialSchema = ({ bookingFields, view, translateFn }: CommonParams) => {
315	  const schema = bookingResponses.unwrap().partial().and(catchAllSchema);
316	  return preprocess({ schema, bookingFields, isPartialSchema: true, view, translateFn });
317	};

319	// Should be used when we know that not all fields responses are present
320	// - Can happen when we are parsing the prefill query string
321	// - Can happen when we are parsing a booking's responses (which was created before we added a new required field)
322	export default function getBookingResponsesSchema({ bookingFields, view, translateFn }: CommonParams) {
323	  const schema = bookingResponses.and(z.record(z.any()));
324	  return preprocess({ schema, bookingFields, isPartialSchema: false, view, translateFn });
```

```ts
export function isCancellationReasonRequired(
  setting: CancellationReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}
```

This is the most important finding for mirroring to reschedules — **reschedule reasons already piggyback on the `cancellationReason` field/pipeline** using a `$RCH$` string-prefix marker, rather than a separate field, because reschedules internally cancel-and-recreate the booking:


```ts
  if (!cancellationReason) return "";
  const sanitized = cancellationReason.startsWith("$RCH$")
    ? cancellationReason.substring(5).trim()
    : cancellationReason.trim();
  return `${t("cancellation_reason")}:\n${sanitized}`;
```
- `packages/emails/src/templates/BaseScheduledEmail.tsx` (lines 87–99): picks the i18n label based on the prefix:

```tsx
    label={t(

        : "cancellation_reason"
    )}
    description={
      !!props.calEvent.cancellationReason && props.calEvent.cancellationReason.replace("$RCH$", "")
    } // Removing flag to distinguish reschedule from cancellation
    withSpacer
  />
)}
```

- Webhooks reuse the same `evt.cancellationReason` field (set in `handleCancelBooking.ts` line 275) inside the `CalendarEvent` payload sent via `sendPayload`.

**Implication for mirroring:** a reschedule-reason-requirement feature does not need new email/webhook/UI surfacing plumbing — it already exists via the `$RCH$`-prefixed `cancellationReason` value. export function isCancellationReasonRequired(
```ts
  setting: CancellationReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;

  switch (requirement) {
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH:
      return false;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH:
      return true;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY:
      return isHost;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY:
      return !isHost;
    default:
      return false;
  }
}
```

## 5. `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` — `Booking` model

Relevant `Booking` fields (lines ~862-894), quoted:
```prisma
cancellationReason     String?
rejectionReason        String?
reassignReason         String?
```
**There is no `rescheduleReason` column on `Booking`.** The reschedule reason is never stored under its own name in the DB — it is always folded into the existing `cancellationReason` string column (either directly, as in `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`, or with a `$RCH$` prefix marker in the seated/email-task code paths, or via `createBooking.ts:236` when a booking is created from a reschedule). This is a key architectural point: there is no dedicated persisted field to compare against for "did the user supply a reschedule reason," only the shared `cancellationReason` text (optionally prefixed).

For comparison, the new **EventType**-level enum added for the cancellation-reason feature (line 287):
```prisma
requiresCancellationReason    CancellationReasonRequirement? @default(MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY)
```
with the enum itself defined via migration `packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/migration.sql`:
```sql
CREATE TYPE "public"."CancellationReasonRequirement" AS ENUM ('MANDATORY_BOTH', 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY', 'MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY', 'OPTIONAL_BOTH');
ALTER TABLE "public"."EventType" ADD COLUMN "requiresCancellationReason" "public"."CancellationReasonRequirement" DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```
There is also an unrelated `cancellationReason` field on `InternalNotePreset` (schema.prisma line 2274) used for canned cancellation-note presets — not relevant to Booking/reschedule.

Note: `specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/CLAUDE.md` (the spec doc for the existing feature) explicitly states under "Don't": *"Don't modify reschedule reason behavior (out of scope)"*, and `design.md`'s "Out of Scope" section lists *"Reschedule reason configuration (separate feature)"* — confirming this was deliberately deferred and is exactly the gap the new `requiresRescheduleReason` feature should fill.

```ts
export function isCancellationReasonRequired(
  setting: CancellationReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;
  switch (requirement) {
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH: return false;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH: return true;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY: return isHost;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY: return !isHost;
    default: return false;
  }
}
```
  This is used both server-side in `handleCancelBooking.ts:156-159` and client-side in `apps/web/components/booking/CancelBooking.tsx:167-172` (with `missingRequiredReason` gating the submit button at line 172, and the label switching between `cancellation_reason` / `cancellation_reason_optional_label` at line 229). An analogous `isRescheduleReasonRequired` helper + prop-threading through `RescheduleDialog.tsx` (client-side gating) and `requestReschedule.handler.ts` (server-side enforcement, plus Flow B's `getBookingFields.ts`/`getBookingResponsesSchema.ts` path) is the mirrored shape needed for the new feature.

## 5. `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` — `Booking` model

Relevant `Booking` fields (lines ~862-894), quoted:
```prisma
cancellationReason     String?
rejectionReason        String?
reassignReason         String?
```
**There is no `rescheduleReason` column on `Booking`.** The reschedule reason is never stored under its own name in the DB — it is always folded into the existing `cancellationReason` string column (either directly, as in `requestReschedule.handler.ts:84`, or with a `$RCH$` prefix marker in the seated/email-task code paths, or via `createBooking.ts:236` when a booking is created from a reschedule). This is a key architectural point: there is no dedicated persisted field to compare against for "did the user supply a reschedule reason," only the shared `cancellationReason` text (optionally prefixed).

For comparison, the new **EventType**-level enum added for the cancellation-reason feature (line 287):
```prisma
requiresCancellationReason    CancellationReasonRequirement? @default(MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY)
```
with the enum itself defined via migration `packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/migration.sql`:
```sql
CREATE TYPE "public"."CancellationReasonRequirement" AS ENUM ('MANDATORY_BOTH', 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY', 'MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY', 'OPTIONAL_BOTH');
ALTER TABLE "public"."EventType" ADD COLUMN "requiresCancellationReason" "public"."CancellationReasonRequirement" DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
```
There is also an unrelated `cancellationReason` field on `InternalNotePreset` (schema.prisma line 2274) used for canned cancellation-note presets — not relevant to Booking/reschedule.

Note: `specs/cancellation-reason-requirement/CLAUDE.md` (the spec doc for the existing feature) explicitly states under "Don't": *"Don't modify reschedule reason behavior (out of scope)"*, and `design.md`'s "Out of Scope" section lists *"Reschedule reason configuration (separate feature)"* — confirming this was deliberately deferred and is exactly the gap the new `requiresRescheduleReason` feature should fill.

```ts
export function isCancellationReasonRequired(
  setting: CancellationReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
  isHost: boolean
): boolean {
  const requirement = setting ?? CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY;
  switch (requirement) {
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.OPTIONAL_BOTH: return false;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_BOTH: return true;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY: return isHost;
    case CancellationReasonRequirement.MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY: return !isHost;
    default: return false;
  }
}
```

````markdown
# Issue #11: Require a reason when a booking is rescheduled

## Context

Issue #11 (https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/issues/11) points out that Event Types can already force a cancellation reason via `CancellationReasonRequirement` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149`, `EventType.requiresCancellationReason`, enforced in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:157-166`), but there is no equivalent for reschedules — `rescheduleReason` is always optional. The issue asks to mirror the cancellation pattern: a new enum + `EventType` column, an Advanced-tab dropdown, and validation that rejects an empty reason.

**Scope clarified with the user:** Cal.diy actually has two different "reschedule" code paths:
- **Flow A — "Request Reschedule"** (`apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx` → `viewer.bookings.requestReschedule` → `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`): the **host** cancels the booking and asks the attendee to pick a new time. This is host-only (`isBookingOrganizer` check).
- **Flow B — actual reschedule submission** (picking a new slot via the booking form, `packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingFields.ts`): can be done by host or attendee, but has no "who is submitting" context today.

The user confirmed the request is specifically about **Flow A**: today clicking "Request Reschedule" always works even with an empty "Reason for reschedule request" box; they want that button disabled/blocked until a reason is typed, exactly like the Cancel dialog already blocks "Cancel Event" until a cancellation reason is entered (`apps/web/components/booking/CancelBooking.tsx:172,177-178,279`). **Flow B is out of scope for this change.**

Because Flow A can only ever be triggered by the booking's host, the new enum is still implemented with the full 4 values for fidelity with the issue's ask and for forward compatibility, but in practice `isHost` is always `true` in this flow, so `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` and `MANDATORY_BOTH` both require a reason, `OPTIONAL_BOTH` never does, and `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` never does (no attendee-initiated path exists yet).

## Implementation Plan

Per this repo's PR-size rules (<500 lines / <10 files per PR), split into 4 sequential PRs, in dependency order.

### PR 1 — Schema + migration (⚠️ requires explicit confirmation before running — CLAUDE.md flags schema changes as "ask first")

- `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`: add a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum next to `CancellationReasonRequirement` (line ~149-154), with the same 4 values (`MANDATORY_BOTH`, `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`, `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY`, `OPTIONAL_BOTH`). Add `requiresRescheduleReason RescheduleReasonRequirement? @default(MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY)` on `EventType`, next to `requiresCancellationReason` (line ~287).
- New migration `packages/prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_add_reschedule_reason_require/migration.sql`, mirroring `packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/migration.sql`:
  ```sql
  -- CreateEnum
  CREATE TYPE "public"."RescheduleReasonRequirement" AS ENUM ('MANDATORY_BOTH', 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY', 'MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY', 'OPTIONAL_BOTH');

  -- AlterTable
  ALTER TABLE "public"."EventType" ADD COLUMN "requiresRescheduleReason" "public"."RescheduleReasonRequirement" DEFAULT 'MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY';
  ```
- Run `yarn prisma generate` after this lands so `RescheduleReasonRequirement` is available from `@calcom/prisma/enums`.

### PR 2 — Backend validation for Flow A

- New file `packages/features/bookings/lib/rescheduleReason.ts`, mirroring `packages/features/bookings/lib/cancellationReason.ts` exactly (same switch shape, using `RescheduleReasonRequirement`):
  ```ts
  export function isRescheduleReasonRequired(
    setting: RescheduleReasonRequirement | null | undefined,
    isHost: boolean
  ): boolean { /* same 4-branch switch as isCancellationReasonRequired */ }
  ```
````

  2. Mandatory for host only
  3. Mandatory for attendee only
  4. Optional for both

3. Enforce the selected requirement during rescheduling. For example, if the event type is set to "Mandatory for attendee only," an attendee should not be able to complete a reschedule with an empty reason, while the host should not be required by that setting.

4. Surface the submitted reschedule reason in the appropriate places where the equivalent cancellation reason is currently surfaced.

```text
441	  userId: number | null;

443	}): Promise<void> {
444	  if (!rescheduleUid || !eventType) {
445	    return; // Not a reschedule, skip validation
446	  }
447

449	  const actualRescheduleUid = bookingSeat ? bookingSeat.booking.uid : rescheduleUid;

451	  if (!actualRescheduleUid) {

453	  }

457	      actualRescheduleUid,

460

463	      userId && originalRescheduledBooking.userId && userId === originalRescheduledBooking.userId;
464

466	    const { minimumRescheduleNotice } = originalRescheduledBooking.eventType || {};
```

```text
375	};

377	// TODO: Move preprocess of `booking.responses` to FormBuilder schema as that is going to parse the fields supported by FormBuilder
378	// It allows anyone using FormBuilder to get the same preprocessing automatically
379	function preprocess<T extends z.ZodType>({
380	  schema,
381	  bookingFields,
382	  isPartialSchema,
383	  view: currentView,
384	  checkOptional = false,
385	  translateFn,
386	}: CommonParams & {
387	  schema: T;
388	  // It is useful when we want to prefill the responses with the partial values. Partial can be in 2 ways
389	  // - Not all required fields are need to be provided for prefill.
390	  // - Even a field response itself can be partial so the content isn't validated e.g. a field with type="phone" can be given a partial phone number(e.g. Specifying the country code like +91)
391	  isPartialSchema: boolean;
392	  checkOptional?: boolean;
393	}): z.ZodType<z.infer<T>, z.infer<T>, z.infer<T>> {
394	  const log = logger.getSubLogger({ prefix: ["getBookingResponsesSchema"] });
395	  const preprocessed = z.preprocess(
396	    (responses) => {
397	      const parsedResponses = z.record(z.any()).nullable().parse(responses) || {};
398	      const newResponses = {} as typeof parsedResponses;
399	      // if eventType has been deleted, we won't have bookingFields and thus we can't preprocess or validate them.
400	      if (!bookingFields) return parsedResponses;
401	      bookingFields.forEach((field) => {
402	        const value = parsedResponses[field.name];
403	        if (value === undefined) {
404	          // If there is no response for the field, then we don't need to do any processing
405	          return;
406	        }
407	        const views = field.views;
408	        const isFieldApplicableToCurrentView =
409	          currentView === "ALL_VIEWS" ? true : views ? views.find((view) => view.id === currentView) : true;
410	        if (!isFieldApplicableToCurrentView) {
411	          // If the field is not applicable in the current view, then we don't need to do any processing
412	          return;
413	        }
414	
415	        try {
416	          newResponses[field.name] = preprocessField({ field, value, isPartialSchema, log });
417	        } catch (e) {
418	          if (!isPartialSchema) {
419	            throw e;
420	          }
421	          const errorMessage = e instanceof Error ? e.message : "preprocessing failed";
422	          const invalidFieldName = field.name;
423	          // Remove invalid field like it never existed in the first place
424	          delete parsedResponses[invalidFieldName];
425	          console.warn(`Skipped invalid field during preprocessing: ${invalidFieldName} (${errorMessage})`);
426	        }
427	      });
428	
429	      return {
430	        ...parsedResponses,
431	        ...newResponses,
432	      };
433	    },
434	    schema.superRefine(async (responses, ctx) => {
435	      if (!bookingFields) {
436	        // if eventType has been deleted, we won't have bookingFields and thus we can't validate the responses.
437	        return;
438	      }
439	
440	      const attendeePhoneNumberField = bookingFields.find((field) => field.name === "attendeePhoneNumber");
441	      const isAttendeePhoneNumberFieldHidden = attendeePhoneNumberField?.hidden;
442	
443	      const emailField = bookingFields.find((field) => field.name === "email");
444	      const isEmailFieldHidden = !!emailField?.hidden;
445	
446	      // To prevent using user's session email as attendee's email, we set email to empty string
447	      if (isEmailFieldHidden && !isAttendeePhoneNumberFieldHidden) {
448	        responses["email"] = "";
449	      }
450	
451	      for (const bookingField of bookingFields) {
452	        const value = responses[bookingField.name];
453	        const views = bookingField.views;
454	        const isFieldApplicableToCurrentView =
455	          currentView === "ALL_VIEWS" ? true : views ? views.find((view) => view.id === currentView) : true;
456	        let hidden = bookingField.hidden;
457	        const numOptions = bookingField.options?.length ?? 0;
458	        if (bookingField.hideWhenJustOneOption) {
459	          hidden = hidden || numOptions <= 1;
460	        }
461	        let isRequired = false;
462	        // If the field is hidden, then it can never be required
463	        if (!hidden && isFieldApplicableToCurrentView) {
464	          isRequired = checkOptional || !!bookingField.required;
465	        }
466	
467	        if ((isPartialSchema || !isRequired) && value === undefined) {
468	          continue;
469	        }
470	
471	        // For partial schemas, use a proxy ctx to capture issues
472	        const { fieldZodCtx, state } = buildFieldZodCtx({
473	          zodCtx: ctx,
474	          isPartialSchema,
475	        });
476	
477	        let superRefineError = false;
478	        try {
479	          await superRefineField({
480	            field: bookingField,
481	            value,
482	            isPartialSchema,
483	            isRequired,
484	            checkOptional,
485	            zodCtx: fieldZodCtx,
486	            translateFn,
487	            responses,
488	          });
489	        } catch (e) {
490	          if (!isPartialSchema) {
491	            throw e;
492	          }
493	          superRefineError = true;
494	        }
495	
496	        // For partial schemas, remove invalid fields from responses
497	        const issues = state?.issues ?? [];
498	        if (isPartialSchema && (superRefineError || issues.length > 0)) {
499	          delete responses[bookingField.name];
500	          console.warn(
501	            `Partial prefill: skipped field '${bookingField.name}' due to ${issues.length} validation error(s)`
502	          );
503	        }
504	      }
505	    })
506	  );
507	  if (isPartialSchema) {
508	    // Query Params can be completely invalid, try to preprocess as much of it in correct format but in worst case simply don't prefill instead of crashing
509	    return preprocessed.catch((res?: { error?: unknown[] }) => {
510	      console.error("Failed to validate query params, prefilling will be skipped entirely", res?.error);
511	      return {};
512	    });
513	  }
514	  return preprocessed;
515	}
516
```

```text
208	export function shouldShowPendingActions(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
209	  const { isPending, isUpcoming, isCancelled } = context;
210	  return isPending && isUpcoming && !isCancelled;
211	}

213	export function shouldShowEditActions(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
214	  const { isPending, isTabRecurring, isRecurring, isCancelled } = context;
215	  return !isPending && !(isTabRecurring && isRecurring) && !isCancelled;
216	}

218	export function shouldShowRecurringCancelAction(context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
219	  const { isTabRecurring, isRecurring } = context;
220	  return isTabRecurring && isRecurring;
221	}

224	  const { booking, isPending, isUpcoming, isCancelled, isRejected } = context;
225	  const hasDropdown = shouldShowEditActions(context);
226	  return !booking.report && !hasDropdown && (isCancelled || isRejected || (isPending && isUpcoming));
227	}

229	export function isActionDisabled(actionId: string, context: BookingActionContext): boolean {
230	  const {
231	    booking,
232	    isBookingInPast,
233	    isDisabledRescheduling,
234	    isDisabledCancelling,
235	    isAttendee,
236	    isCancelled,
237	    isRejected,
238	  } = context;
239	
240	  switch (actionId) {
241	    case "reschedule":
242	    case "reschedule_request":
243	      // Only apply minimum reschedule notice restriction if user is NOT the organizer
244	      // If user is an attendee (or not authenticated), apply the restriction
245	      const isUserOrganizer =
246	        !isAttendee &&
247	        booking.loggedInUser?.userId &&
248	        booking.user?.id &&
249	        booking.loggedInUser.userId === booking.user.id;
250	      const isWithinMinimumNotice =
251	        !isUserOrganizer &&
252	        isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice(
253	          new Date(booking.startTime),
254	          booking.eventType.minimumRescheduleNotice ?? null
255	        );
256	      return (
257	        isCancelled ||
258	        isRejected ||
259	        (isBookingInPast && !booking.eventType.allowReschedulingPastBookings) ||
260	        isDisabledRescheduling ||
261	        isWithinMinimumNotice
262	      );
263	    case "cancel":
264	      return isDisabledCancelling || isBookingInPast || isCancelled || isRejected;
265	    case "view_recordings":
266	      return !(isBookingInPast && booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED && context.isCalVideoLocation);
267	    case "meeting_session_details":
268	      return !(isBookingInPast && booking.status === BookingStatus.ACCEPTED && context.isCalVideoLocation);
269	    case "charge_card":
270	      return context.cardCharged;
271	    case "reassign":
272	    case "change_location":
273	    case "add_members":
274	      return isBookingInPast || isCancelled || isRejected;
275	    default:
276	      return false;
277	  }
278	}
279	
280	export function getActionLabel(actionId: string, context: BookingActionContext): string {
281	  const { isTabRecurring, isRecurring, attendeeList, cardCharged, t } = context;
282	
283	  switch (actionId) {
284	    case "reject":
285	      return (isTabRecurring || context.isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("reject_all") : t("reject");
286	    case "confirm":
287	      return (isTabRecurring || context.isTabUnconfirmed) && isRecurring ? t("confirm_all") : t("confirm");
288	    case "cancel":
289	      return isTabRecurring && isRecurring ? t("cancel_all_remaining") : t("cancel_event");
290	    case "no_show":
291	      return attendeeList.length === 1 && attendeeList[0].noShow
292	        ? t("unmark_as_no_show")
293	        : t("mark_as_no_show");
294	    case "charge_card":
295	      return cardCharged ? t("no_show_fee_charged") : t("collect_no_show_fee");
296	    default:
297	      return t(actionId);
298	  }
299	}
```

## 1. Does the reschedule flow already know if the requester is the host?

Yes — partially, and only for one narrow purpose (minimum-notice bypass), not for form-field requirements.

In `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts`, the `handler` function (the actual `handleNewBooking`-equivalent entry point used for both new bookings and reschedules) calls a helper `validateRescheduleRestrictions` **before** building the booking-fields schema:

```
packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:435-484
async function validateRescheduleRestrictions({
  rescheduleUid, userId, eventType,
}): Promise<void> {
  ...
  const originalRescheduledBooking = await getOriginalRescheduledBooking(
    actualRescheduleUid, !!eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot
  );

  // Check if user is the organizer
  const isUserOrganizer =
    userId && originalRescheduledBooking.userId && userId === originalRescheduledBooking.userId;   // lines 462-463

  const { minimumRescheduleNotice } = originalRescheduledBooking.eventType || {};
  if (
    !isUserOrganizer &&
    isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice(originalRescheduledBooking.startTime, minimumRescheduleNotice ?? null)
  ) {
    throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 403, message: "Rescheduling is not allowed within the minimum notice period before the event" });
  }
}
```

Called from `handler` at line 529:

```
packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:486-538
async function handler(this: RegularBookingService, input: BookingHandlerInput, deps, ...) {
  const { bookingData: rawBookingData, userId, ... } = input;
  ...
  const eventType = await getEventType({ eventTypeId: rawBookingData.eventTypeId, eventTypeSlug: ... });

  // Early validation: Check reschedule restrictions if rescheduling

    rescheduleUid: rawBookingData.rescheduleUid,

  ...
```

So `userId` (the logged-in session user id, or `null`/`-1` sentinel when anonymous — see below) **is** available at this point, and it **is** compared against `originalRescheduledBooking.userId` (the original booking's/event's owner) to compute `isUserOrganizer`. However, this boolean is used *only* to skip the minimum-reschedule-notice check — it is computed and discarded inside `validateRescheduleRestrictions`, never returned or threaded into `getEventType`/`getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields`/`getBookingDataSchema`, which are called afterward with no host-context at all.

Later in the same `handler`, in the section that fires reschedule notification emails, there's a related-but-different computation using `reqBody.rescheduledBy` (an email, not the session id) compared to the attendee's email:

```

```
(and again at line 2542). This is used purely to pick email wording ("you rescheduled" vs "attendee rescheduled"), not for any required-field logic. Note it compares against `bookerEmail` (the attendee), not the organizer's email — but `organizerUser` (which carries `.email`) is in scope in that same function (e.g. line 1154, `1593` `organizerUser` is passed into `handleSeats`), so an analogous `reqBody.rescheduledBy === organizerUser.email` check is trivially reachable in the same scope.

## 2. Is there a session for reschedule submissions, or is it anonymous?

Both — it depends on how the person arrived, and the session is only sometimes present.

The public booking API route that ultimately calls `RegularBookingService.createBooking` (and thus `handler` above) does fetch a server session:

```
apps/web/pages/api/book/event.ts:42,49-58
const session = await getServerSession({ req });
...
const regularBookingService = getRegularBookingService();
const booking = await regularBookingService.createBooking({
  bookingData: req.body,
  bookingMeta: {
    userId: session?.user?.id || -1,     // <-- sentinel -1 when NOT logged in
    hostname: req.headers.host || "",
    forcedSlug: req.headers["x-cal-force-slug"] as string | undefined,
    traceContext: req.traceContext,
  },
});
```

So `input.userId` in `RegularBookingService.handler` is `session?.user?.id` if there's a valid NextAuth session cookie on the request, otherwise `-1`. This means:
- If a logged-in host (or a logged-in attendee-with-an-account) submits the reschedule form while authenticated, `userId` will be their real id, and `isUserOrganizer` (line 462-463) will correctly evaluate to `true`/`false`.
- If the person is NOT logged in (the overwhelmingly common case — a guest/attendee reschedules via an emailed link with no Cal.diy account), `userId` is `-1`, which can never match `originalRescheduledBooking.userId`, so `isUserOrganizer` is always `false` for anonymous requesters — indistinguishable from "confirmed non-host."

Separately (and more usefully), there is an **email-based** channel analogous to `cancelledBy` in `handleCancelBooking.ts`: `reqBody.rescheduledBy`. This is threaded through the whole reschedule pipeline:
- `packages/features/bookings/lib/bookingCreateBodySchema.ts:14` — `rescheduledBy: z.string().email(...).optional()` in the request body schema.
- Populated client-side from a `rescheduledBy` URL query param, read in `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx:58-59` (`new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("rescheduledBy")`), stored in Booker's zustand store, read again in `apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useBookings.ts:120`, and mapped into the booking-create payload in `packages/features/bookings/lib/client/booking-event-form/booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.tsx:19,43,77`.
- That query param is set in two known places:
  - `apps/web/lib/reschedule/[uid]/getServerSideProps.ts:194-197` — the dashboard "reschedule" redirect page sets `rescheduledBy = rescheduledBy(query) ?? session?.user?.email` and forwards it into the redirect URL to the public booking page. This is a session-derived email (of whoever is logged into the dashboard).
  - `packages/lib/CalEventParser.ts:403-436` (`getRescheduleLink`) — used when building the "Reschedule" link inside *attendee-facing* notification emails: `rescheduledBy: attendee?.email` (line 433). Organizer-facing manage links call it without an `attendee`, so `rescheduledBy` stays unset there.

So: for a truly anonymous public-form reschedule with no query param and no session, there is **no** signal at all (neither `userId` nor `rescheduledBy`) — the requester is fully unauthenticated and indistinguishable except via the "who is this booking for" answers they type into the form itself (the `bookerEmail` field). For reschedules that originate from the dashboard `reschedule` action or from an attendee notification email, `rescheduledBy` carries a real email that's already compared against `bookerEmail` (line 2041/2542) — extending that comparison to `organizerUser.email` would need no schema changes, since `reqBody.rescheduledBy` is already validated as a real email in `bookingCreateBodySchema.ts:14`.

## 3. `getBookingFields.ts` — full signature and callers; can "isHost" be threaded through?

Full function (`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingFields.ts:34-60`):

```ts
export const getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields = ({
  bookingFields,
  disableGuests,
  isOrgTeamEvent = false,
  disableBookingTitle,
  customInputs,
  metadata,
}: {
  bookingFields: Fields | EventType["bookingFields"];
  disableGuests: boolean;
  isOrgTeamEvent?: boolean;
  disableBookingTitle?: boolean;
  customInputs: EventTypeCustomInput[] | z.infer<typeof customInputSchema>[];
  metadata: EventType["metadata"] | z.infer<typeof EventTypeMetaDataSchema>;
}) => {
  const parsedMetaData = EventTypeMetaDataSchema.parse(metadata || {});
  const parsedBookingFields = eventTypeBookingFields.parse(bookingFields || []);
  const parsedCustomInputs = customInputSchema.array().parse(customInputs || []);
  return ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields({
    bookingFields: parsedBookingFields,
    disableGuests,
    isOrgTeamEvent,
    disableBookingTitle,
    additionalNotesRequired: parsedMetaData?.additionalNotesRequired || false,   // line 57
    customInputs: parsedCustomInputs,
  });
};
```

`additionalNotesRequired` is a plain boolean pulled out of `EventTypeMetaDataSchema.parse(metadata)` — i.e. it's an **event-type-level static setting** (an admin toggle stored in the event type's metadata JSON), not derived from who is booking. It then flows into `ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields` where it directly sets `required: additionalNotesRequired` on the `notes` system field (line 196). There is no equivalent per-request/per-booker input anywhere in this call chain — the function has zero knowledge of who is submitting the form.

Callers, none of which pass or have access to an "isHost"/"bookerIsOrganizer" concept:
- Server, actual booking submission path: `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getEventType.ts:27` → `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields({ ...eventType, isOrgTeamEvent })`, called from `getEventType()` which is invoked in `RegularBookingService.handler` at line 523-526 with only `{ eventTypeId, eventTypeSlug }` — no `userId` passed in.

  ```ts
    view: "booking" | "reschedule";
    bookingFields: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields>>;
  ```

- `getBookingResponsesSchema` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema.ts:13,322-325`) takes `CommonParams = { bookingFields, view, translateFn }`. Inside `preprocess`'s `superRefine`, the only thing that decides `isRequired` is:

  ```
  if (!hidden && isFieldApplicableToCurrentView) {
  ```

  i.e. it reads the static `required` flag baked onto the field object at build time. There is no hook here for "who is submitting."

**Feasibility conclusion:** Threading `isHost` through `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields`/`getBookingDataSchema`/`getBookingResponsesSchema` is architecturally invasive (their signatures are shared by many non-reschedule, non-request-scoped callers — event-type CRUD, public-event page rendering, API v2 output). I have gathered sufficient evidence across the codebase. Here is my full report.

## Summary of findings

There is already **one clear precedent** for detecting "is the requester the host" during an actual reschedule (in `RegularBookingService.ts`'s `validateRescheduleRestrictions`), and a **second, richer signal** (`rescheduledBy` email) that is threaded all the way from the dashboard/email links through the booking form into the booking-creation handler. Neither signal is currently wired into `getBookingFields.ts` / `getBookingResponsesSchema.ts`, which are host-agnostic by design. Below is the detail per question.

---

### 1. Does the reschedule-handling code know if the requester is host vs. attendee?

Yes — in `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts`, function `validateRescheduleRestrictions` (lines 435-484), called from `handler` at lines 529-538 (before booking data/schema are even built):

```ts
// packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:456-463
const originalRescheduledBooking = await getOriginalRescheduledBooking(
  actualRescheduleUid,
  !!eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot
);

// Check if user is the organizer
const isUserOrganizer =
  userId && originalRescheduledBooking.userId && userId === originalRescheduledBooking.userId;
```

`userId` here is `input.userId` from `BookingHandlerInput`/`CreateBookingMeta` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/dto/types.d.ts:34`, `userId?: number`), i.e. the **logged-in session user id**, if any, at the time the booking-creation API call is made. This is used today only to decide whether to enforce `minimumRescheduleNotice` (line 468: `!isUserOrganizer && isWithinMinimumRescheduleNotice(...)`) — it is not threaded any further into booking-fields/validation logic.

The `handler` function itself (`RegularBookingService.ts:486-538`) receives `userId` directly as a top-level destructured input (line 494), so it's available at the very top of the reschedule-handling code path, before `getEventType`, `getBookingData`, or `getBookingDataSchema` are invoked (lines 523-549).

---

### 2. Is a session/user id or email available for reschedule submissions the way it is for cancel?

**Yes, but conditionally** — the API route that receives reschedule (and new-booking) submissions does fetch a server session:

```ts
// apps/web/pages/api/book/event.ts:42, 49-58
const session = await getServerSession({ req });
...
const regularBookingService = getRegularBookingService();
const booking = await regularBookingService.createBooking({
  bookingData: req.body,
  bookingMeta: {
    userId: session?.user?.id || -1,
    ...
  },
});
```

Note the `-1` sentinel: if nobody is logged in (the common case — an attendee clicking a booking-confirmation-email link is typically **not authenticated**), `userId` becomes `-1`, which can never equal a real organizer id, so `isUserOrganizer` in `validateRescheduleRestrictions` is deterministically `false` for anonymous reschedulers. So: the session *is* available when it exists, but a plain attendee reschedule is very often anonymous/unauthenticated — `userId` alone is not a reliable "is this an attendee" signal, only a reliable "is this a specific logged-in user" signal.

There is a **second, more robust signal** that behaves like `cancelledBy` in `handleCancelBooking.ts` (`userId === cancelledBy` style): `reqBody.rescheduledBy` (an email string), which is already present in scope in `RegularBookingService.ts` alongside `organizerUser` and `bookerEmail`:

```ts
// packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:2041 (and again at :2542)
isRescheduledByBooker: reqBody.rescheduledBy === bookerEmail,
```

This is the reverse of what we want (checks against the *attendee's* email, used only to pick email-template wording), but it proves `reqBody.rescheduledBy`, `bookerEmail`, and `organizerUser.email` are all in scope in the same function body (see `RegularBookingService.ts:1591-1618`, where `organizerUser`, `bookerEmail`, and `reqBody.rescheduledBy` are passed together into `handleSeats`). Computing `reqBody.rescheduledBy === organizerUser.email` (an "isRescheduledByOrganizer" analogue to `isCancellationUserHost`) would be architecturally trivial there.

Where does `rescheduledBy` come from?
- `bookingCreateBodySchema.ts:14`: `rescheduledBy: z.string().email().optional()` — optional, so it can simply be absent (undefined) for anonymous attendee reschedules that don't originate from a dashboard/tracked link.
- It's set server-side when a **dashboard "reschedule" action** redirects into the booking page: `apps/web/lib/reschedule/[uid]/getServerSideProps.ts:194`: `const currentUserEmail = rescheduledBy ?? session?.user?.email;` then appended as a query param (`?rescheduledBy=...`) on the redirect to the actual event/Booker URL.
- It's also set in attendee-facing calendar/email "Reschedule" links via `packages/lib/CalEventParser.ts:403-436` (`getRescheduleLink`), which does `rescheduledBy: attendee?.email` — i.e. the attendee's own email is stamped into the link, but only when an `attendee` is passed (organizer-facing "manage" links at line 284 call `getRescheduleLink({ calEvent })` with no attendee, so `rescheduledBy` stays undefined there).
- Client-side, the query param is read in `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx:58-59` (`new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("rescheduledBy")`), stored in the Booker store, read by `useBookings.ts:120`, and mapped into the mutation body by `packages/features/bookings/lib/client/booking-event-form/booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.tsx:19,43,77`.

**Conclusion for #2**: A logged-in session (`userId`) is available at the API boundary but frequently absent for genuine attendee reschedules. A better, already-plumbed identity signal is the optional `rescheduledBy` email, which for host-initiated reschedules (via the dashboard "reschedule" button) carries the host's session email, and for attendee-initiated reschedules from calendar-invite links carries the attendee's email. Both signals converge in the same `RegularBookingService.handler` scope alongside `organizerUser.email`.

### 3. `getBookingFields.ts` full review — is host-context threadable?

Full function signature (`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingFields.ts:34-60`):

```ts
export const getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields = ({
  bookingFields,
  disableGuests,
  isOrgTeamEvent = false,
  disableBookingTitle,
  customInputs,
  metadata,
}: {
  bookingFields: Fields | EventType["bookingFields"];
  disableGuests: boolean;
  isOrgTeamEvent?: boolean;
  disableBookingTitle?: boolean;
  customInputs: EventTypeCustomInput[] | z.infer<typeof customInputSchema>[];
  metadata: EventType["metadata"] | z.infer<typeof EventTypeMetaDataSchema>;
}) => {
  const parsedMetaData = EventTypeMetaDataSchema.parse(metadata || {});
  ...
  return ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields({
    ...
    additionalNotesRequired: parsedMetaData?.additionalNotesRequired || false,
    ...
  });
};
```

`additionalNotesRequired` is a **plain boolean** pulled out of `EventTypeMetaDataSchema.parse(metadata)` — it's an event-type-level setting stored in `EventType.metadata`, with zero awareness of who the current requester is. It's threaded into `ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields` (line 62-76) which uses it directly as `required: additionalNotesRequired` on the `notes` system field (line 196). By contrast, `rescheduleReason` is hardcoded `required: false` (line 228) with a `views: [{ id: "reschedule" }]` gate (lines 229-234) — the `views` mechanism only controls **field visibility per view**, not conditional `required`-ness.

**Callers** (none pass or could easily pass an isHost/bookerIsOrganizer flag without a signature change):
- Server-side, used to build `bookingFields` before schema validation:
  - `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/getEventType.ts:27` — `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields({ ...eventType, isOrgTeamEvent })`. This is called from `RegularBookingService.handler` (`getEventType({ eventTypeId, eventTypeSlug })`, line 523-526) with **no userId/session parameter at all** — `getEventType`'s own signature (`getEventType.ts:8-14`) only takes `eventTypeId`/`eventTypeSlug`.
  - `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:343,565,772` — used to build the public/booker-facing event payload (client fetches this via tRPC `viewer.public.event`), also no host param.
  - `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getEventTypeById.ts:224`, `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/bookingFieldsManager.ts:34`, `apps/web/lib/booking.ts:131` — event-type settings/editor pages, again no host param.
- The resulting `bookingFields` then flow into validation: `packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingDataSchema.ts:7-17` (`view`, `bookingFields` only) → `packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema.ts` (`CommonParams = { bookingFields, view, translateFn }`, line 13) → inside `preprocess`'s `superRefine`, the only driver of "is this field required" is `isRequired = checkOptional || !!bookingField.required` (line 464) — a static flag baked into the field object **before** this function ever runs.

**Architectural conclusion**: There is no seam anywhere in this pipeline (`getEventType` → `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields` → `getBookingDataSchema` → `getBookingResponsesSchema`) that carries a request-specific "isHost" concept — everything here is purely a function of the **event type's static configuration**. To make `rescheduleReason.required` conditional on host-vs-attendee, you would need one of:
- (a) Compute `isHost`/`isRescheduledByOrganizer` in `RegularBookingService.handler` (where `userId`, `organizerUser.email`, `reqBody.rescheduledBy`, and `originalRescheduledBooking` are already in scope — see `validateRescheduleRestrictions`, lines 461-463) and mutate/override the `rescheduleReason` field's `required` property on the `eventType.bookingFields` array right before calling `getBookingDataSchema` (`RegularBookingService.ts:540-543`) — a **local, non-breaking change**, since none of the four functions' signatures need to change.
- (b) A larger change: add an `isHost`/`bookerIsOrganizer` param to `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields`, `ensureBookingInputsHaveSystemFields`, `getBookingDataSchema`, and `CommonParams` in `getBookingResponsesSchema.ts`, and pass it through every one of the ~9 callers listed above (several of which — event-type settings pages, public event fetch — have no natural notion of "current booker" at all, since they're not processing a submission).

Option (a) is clearly the lower-risk, more feasible path.

### 4. Does the public booking-page frontend already know "am I the host"?

**No** — searched `packages/features/bookings/Booker/` and `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/`; no `isHost`, `isLoggedInUserHost`, or similar flag exists there. `BookingFields.tsx` (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/BookingFields.tsx`) already special-cases `rescheduleReason` rendering (lines 146-152):

```tsx
if (field.name === SystemField.Enum.rescheduleReason) {
  if (bookingData === null) {
    return null;
  }
  readOnly = false;
}
```

— purely based on whether it's a reschedule (`bookingData !== null`), with no host/attendee branching, and no `isHost`-style prop exists on `BookingFields`'s props type at all. The one place `isHost`-style logic *does* exist client-side is the **post-booking confirmation page** (`bookings-single-view.tsx:175`, `props.isLoggedInUserHost`, sourced server-side from `checkIfUserIsHost(userId)` in `apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.getServerSideProps.tsx:164-182`, where `userId = session?.user?.id`) and in `BookingActionsDropdown.tsx:187` (`booking.loggedInUser.userId === booking.user?.id`) — but that's for the dashboard/manage-booking view, not the Booker/booking-form itself, and is not exposed to the form component. A reschedule-reason feature cannot reuse an existing flag here; one would have to be newly introduced (most naturally server-side, in `getEventType.ts`/`RegularBookingService.ts` per #3, then optionally surfaced to the client via the booking-data response for UI purposes).

### 5. Is there a third, dashboard-initiated "instant reschedule" flow distinct from "Request Reschedule" and the public form?

Yes, confirmed in `apps/web/components/booking/actions/bookingActions.ts:114-143` (`getEditEventActions`): there are **two separate actions** in the bookings-list dropdown:

```ts
{
  id: "reschedule",
  icon: "clock",
  label: t("reschedule_booking"),
  href: `/reschedule/${booking.uid}...`,
  ...
},
{
  id: "reschedule_request",
  icon: "send",
  label: t("send_reschedule_request"),
  ...
},
```

`reschedule_request` opens `RescheduleDialog.tsx` (host-initiated "Request Reschedule" — already known to you). `reschedule` (id `"reschedule"`, label `reschedule_booking`) is a **third, distinct entry point** — it navigates to `/reschedule/[uid]`, whose `getServerSideProps` (`apps/web/lib/reschedule/[uid]/getServerSideProps.ts`) does **not** render its own UI; instead it:
1. Reads the session (`getServerSession`), computes `currentUserEmail = rescheduledBy ?? session?.user?.email` (line 194),
2. For seated events, explicitly checks host/owner status server-side (lines 166-178: `userIsHost` via `eventType.hosts`, `userIsOwnerOfEventType` via `eventType.owner?.id === userId`) and 404s non-hosts lacking a seat reference,
3. **Redirects** to the normal public event booking URL with `?rescheduleUid=...&rescheduledBy=<email>` (lines 181-207).

So architecturally this "instant dashboard reschedule" is **not a separate code path** — it's a redirect wrapper that funnels into the exact same public Booker/booking-form "actual reschedule" flow already identified, just pre-seeding `rescheduledBy` with the current dashboard session's email (host's email, if the host clicked it) as a query param that survives into the final `POST /api/book/event` submission (via `BookerWebWrapper.tsx:58-59,72,82,220` → Booker store → `useBookings.ts:120,264` → `booking-to-mutation-input-mapper.tsx:19,43,77` → `reqBody.rescheduledBy`). This is exactly the mechanism described in #2 that could serve as an "is host" signal for a reschedule-reason feature, since a host-clicked `reschedule` action reliably stamps the host's own email into `rescheduledBy` before the booking form is ever rendered.

No other reschedule entry points were found (`EditLocationDialog` only handles location changes, not time; no other admin/dashboard "reschedule" action exists beyond these two).

```markdown
# Issue #11: Require a reason when a booking is rescheduled — Investigation & Plan

## Context

Issue #11 asks to mirror the existing cancellation-reason-requirement feature for reschedules: a `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum + `EventType.requiresRescheduleReason` column (same 4 values/default as cancellation), a dropdown in Event Type → Advanced next to "Require cancellation reason," validation that rejects an empty reason "shaped like" `handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`, and surfacing the reason wherever the cancellation reason already appears.

**Why this reset happened:** the previous pass assumed "the reschedule path" meant only the host-initiated "Request Reschedule" dialog. Investigation now shows the codebase actually has **three reschedule entry points**, and the issue's own example ("Mandatory for attendee only" should block an attendee, not the host) only has real meaning on one of them. This document lays out all three, maps each of the issue's four requirements to concrete files, and flags where the issue and the existing architecture don't cleanly line up — without picking an answer for you.

## The three reschedule entry points

| Flow | Trigger | Who can do it | Does it set a new time? | Backend |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A — Request Reschedule** | "Send Reschedule Request" action in bookings list → `apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx` | **Host only** (`isBookingOrganizer` check) | No — cancels the booking and emails the attendee a link to pick a time later | `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts` |
| **B — Dashboard "Reschedule" link** | "Reschedule" action in bookings list → `/reschedule/[uid]` | Host or attendee (whoever has access to that booking) | No by itself — it's a redirect | `apps/web/lib/reschedule/[uid]/getServerSideProps.ts`: reads session, sets `rescheduledBy` query param, redirects into Flow C's page |
| **C — Public booking-form reschedule submission** | The actual "pick a new time and confirm" step, reached either via Flow B's redirect or directly via an attendee's emailed link with `rescheduleUid` | Host or attendee (or anonymous) | **Yes — this is the actual reschedule** | `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts` (`handler`), same code path as creating a new booking |

Flow B is just a redirect wrapper around Flow C — they share one backend handler. So there are really two independent places validation could live: **Flow A** (host-only, doesn't move the meeting) and **Flow B/C** (host-or-attendee, actually moves the meeting).

## Requirement-by-requirement analysis

### 1. `RescheduleReasonRequirement` enum + `EventType.requiresRescheduleReason` column

- **Cancellation equivalent:** enum `CancellationReasonRequirement` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:149-154`) + `EventType.requiresCancellationReason` (`schema.prisma:287`, `@default(MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY)`) + migration `packages/prisma/migrations/20260115111819_add_cancellation_reason_require/migration.sql`.
- **Files to change:** `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` (new enum + column, same shape); a new migration folder mirroring the one above.
- **In simple terms:** adds a new per-event-type setting slot in the database, defaulting to "mandatory for host only," with no behavior yet.
- **Host/attendee logic:** none — pure data model.
- **Flow(s) touched:** none directly; this is the foundation for #2 and #3.
- **Tests:** none needed for the schema itself; verify `yarn prisma generate` succeeds and the enum shows up in `@calcom/prisma/enums`.

### 2. "Require reschedule reason" dropdown in Event Type → Advanced

- **Cancellation equivalent:** `Controller`+`Select` block in `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:669-706`; saved via the generic `viewer.eventTypes.update` procedure whose zod input schema lives in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/types.ts:153-156`; read back via `packages/features/eventtypes/repositories/eventTypeRepository.ts` (two `select` blocks, lines ~602 and ~882), typed in `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/types.ts:188,370`, defaulted in `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/defaultEvents.ts:92`.
- **Files to change:** the same set, parallel additions for `requiresRescheduleReason`.
- **In simple terms:** lets a host pick the enum value from the UI; it's persisted through the existing generic update endpoint (no handler code change needed — unknown fields spread straight into the Prisma update).
- **Host/attendee logic:** none — this just stores the admin's choice.
- **Flow(s) touched:** none directly (this only affects what value is later read by #3).
- **Tests:** none dedicated; type-check + a manual save/reload check is sufficient, matching how the cancellation dropdown was verified.

### 3. Enforce the requirement during rescheduling — the core of the issue

- **Cancellation equivalent:** server: `handleCancelBooking.ts:153-166` computes `isCancellationUserHost = bookingToDelete.userId === userId || bookingToDelete.user.email === cancelledBy`, then `isCancellationReasonRequired(requiresCancellationReason, isCancellationUserHost)` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/cancellationReason.ts`), and throws if the reason is blank and required. Client: `apps/web/components/booking/CancelBooking.tsx:164-178` mirrors the same computation and sets `disabled={!canCancel}` on the Cancel button so it **cannot be clicked** until a reason is typed, when required.

- **How host vs. attendee is actually determined in each flow:**
  - **Flow A:** hard-coded — only the booking's organizer can call `requestReschedule` at all (`isBookingOrganizer` check in the handler). There is no attendee-initiated version of this action.
  - **Flow B/C:** `RegularBookingService.ts`'s `validateRescheduleRestrictions` (lines ~435-484) already computes `isUserOrganizer = userId && originalRescheduledBooking.userId === userId`, where `userId` is the logged-in session's id (or a `-1` sentinel when the requester isn't logged in — set in `apps/web/pages/api/book/event.ts:49`: `userId: session?.user?.id || -1`). Today this boolean is used **only** to decide whether to skip the minimum-reschedule-notice check, then it's discarded — it is never passed forward to the code that decides whether `rescheduleReason` is required.
  - There is also a `rescheduledBy` field (an email string, threaded via a URL query param — set from the dashboard session's email in `getServerSideProps.ts:194`, or from the attendee's known email when the link comes from a notification email). **This is client-supplied and not verified against the actual request's session** — using it to decide whether a reason is required would let someone spoof `rescheduledBy=<host's email>` in the URL to dodge an "attendee-only" requirement. The session-verified `isUserOrganizer` computation above is the trustworthy equivalent of `handleCancelBooking.ts`'s `bookingToDelete.userId === userId` check and should be used instead, treating "no session" as "not the host" (safe default, same posture as cancellation).

- **Which flow(s) must change to satisfy the issue:** The issue's own example — "if the event type is set to 'Mandatory for attendee only,' an attendee should not be able to complete a reschedule with an empty reason, while the host should not be required" — only has real meaning in **Flow B/C**, since that's the only flow an attendee can trigger at all. Flow A is host-only, so a setting change there would only ever matter for `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY`/`MANDATORY_BOTH` — it cannot, by itself, satisfy the "mandatory for attendee only" behavior the issue describes. **Flow B/C is the flow that must change for the issue to be satisfied; Flow A is a separate, optional parity improvement** (see ambiguity #1 below).

- **A real architecture gap in Flow B/C:** the functions that actually decide and enforce the `required` flag on booking-form fields — `getBookingFieldsWithSystemFields` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingFields.ts:34-60`) and `getBookingResponsesSchema` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/getBookingResponsesSchema.ts`) — are shared by many callers that have nothing to do with an in-flight reschedule request (event-type CRUD, public event-page rendering, API v2 output). Neither function's signature carries any "who is submitting" context today (compare to `additionalNotesRequired`, which is a static per-event-type boolean, not per-submitter). Threading an `isHost` parameter through these shared signatures would be invasive. The narrower fix: compute `isUserOrganizer` once in `RegularBookingService.handler` (where it's already computed for the notice-bypass) and override the `required` value on the already-built `rescheduleReason` field immediately before the Zod schema is constructed, rather than modifying the shared field-building functions.

- **A second gap — client-side UX:** Cancellation's "you can't click Cancel with an empty box" UX works because the page hosting `CancelBooking.tsx` already computes `isHost` server-side (`apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.getServerSideProps.tsx:164-186`) and passes it down as a prop. The Booker/booking-form (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookEventForm/**`, `packages/features/bookings/Booker/**`) that renders Flow B/C's `rescheduleReason` field has **no equivalent signal today** — no `isHost` prop exists anywhere in that component tree. So even with correct server-side rejection, the client can't grey out the submit button or mark the field required for a "mandatory for host" setting without new client-side host-detection plumbing (e.g., comparing `useSession()` against the event owner). This is genuinely new work, not a copy of an existing pattern — contrary to the issue's "Rough scope: Medium... a parallel copy of known-good code" framing.

- **Tests:**
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 15:31:59Z)**_

## 1. What Issue #11 behavior would remain uncovered if we only implement Flow B/C?

The issue's problem statement names two pieces of evidence for the gap: `SystemField.ts:10` (the field exists) and **`apps/web/components/dialog/RescheduleDialog.tsx:23`** (the field is collected but never enforced). If we only enforce in Flow B/C, `RescheduleDialog.tsx` is untouched — the exact file the issue cites as broken stays broken. Concretely: a host who sets `requiresRescheduleReason` to "Mandatory for host only" or "Mandatory for both" could still open "Request Reschedule" and click "Send Reschedule Request" with an empty reason box, no matter what the setting is. The literal symptom described in the issue would still reproduce.

There's a sharper wrinkle here too: Flow A's "Request Reschedule" internally **cancels** the booking (`requestReschedule.handler.ts:80-86`, `bookingRepository.updateBookingStatus({ status: CANCELLED, cancellationReason, ... })`), but that handler never calls `isCancellationReasonRequired` at all. So today, Flow A already bypasses even the *existing* cancellation-reason requirement — a host can send a reschedule request with an empty reason even if `requiresCancellationReason` is set to `MANDATORY_BOTH`. That's a separate, pre-existing gap (not what #11 asks for), but it means "leave Flow A alone" isn't a neutral choice — it's leaving a known-empty validation gap in place on a state-changing, host-only action.

## 2. How would each of the four settings behave if implemented in Flow A (host-only)?

Since `isHost` is unconditionally `true` in Flow A:

| Setting | Effect in Flow A |
|---|---|
| `MANDATORY_BOTH` | Required — button disabled / request rejected until a reason is typed |
| `MANDATORY_HOST_ONLY` | Required — same effect as above (host is always the actor here) |
| `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` | **Never required** — the "attendee" branch of the setting can never fire, because Flow A can't be triggered by an attendee |
| `OPTIONAL_BOTH` | Never required — same observable behavior as `MANDATORY_ATTENDEE_ONLY` in this flow |

So in Flow A alone, only 2 of the 4 enum values ever produce different behavior from today; the other 2 are indistinguishable from "optional." An admin who picks "Mandatory for attendee only" would see **zero effect** if only Flow A were implemented — that setting would be silently inert everywhere. That by itself is evidence Flow A can't be the *whole* answer: the enum's attendee-facing values only mean anything in Flow B/C.

## 3. Does cancellation enforce at every entry point, or at one operation?

At **one operation**. Every UI surface that lets someone cancel a booking — the bookings-list dropdown (`CancelBookingDialog` via `BookingActionsDropdown.tsx`) and the booking-detail page (`bookings-single-view.tsx`) — renders the same `CancelBooking.tsx` component, which posts to the same `/api/cancel` route, which calls the same `handleCancelBooking.ts`. There is no separate "pre-cancel" or "request cancellation" step in the cancellation feature at all — no analogue to Flow A exists for cancellation. The validation (`isCancellationReasonRequired` + `isCancellationUserHost`) is enforced exactly once, at the single point where the booking's status actually changes, regardless of which screen the user came from, and regardless of whether the actor is host or attendee.

This is the strongest architectural evidence for what "mirror the cancellation setting" means: enforce once, at the operation that actually changes the booking, host-or-attendee-aware, reachable from multiple UI entry points. **Flow C is that operation for reschedule** — it's the point where the booking's time actually changes, reachable via an attendee's email link or via the host's dashboard "Reschedule" button (Flow B is just a redirect into it). Flow A isn't "the same kind of thing" cancellation gates — cancellation has no step where you *ask* someone to cancel later; Flow A is a distinct action (send-a-request) that happens to use a cancel-shaped side effect.

## 4. What scope fully satisfies the issue (not minimizing work)?

Strictly by the evidence above, full satisfaction requires **both**:

- **Flow B/C** (the actual reschedule-to-new-slot submission in `RegularBookingService.handler`) — this is the architectural mirror of `handleCancelBooking.ts`: the one place the state change is committed, the only place an attendee participates, and the only place all 4 enum values (including the attendee-facing ones) can ever have an observable effect. Without this, the setting is partially or fully inert depending on its value.
- **Flow A** (`requestReschedule.handler.ts` / `RescheduleDialog.tsx`) — explicitly named by the issue as evidence of the gap, and a state-changing, host-only action whose reason field is demonstrably unenforced today regardless of any setting. Leaving it out means the exact file/line the issue cites as broken stays broken, and a host retains an unconditional bypass.

Both should use the same `isRescheduleReasonRequired(setting, isHost)` helper, mirroring `isCancellationReasonRequired` exactly — with `isHost` hardcoded `true` for Flow A (matching its host-only nature) and derived from a session-verified check (the existing `isUserOrganizer` computation in `validateRescheduleRestrictions`) for Flow B/C. This is a larger scope than the original "smallest copy of known-good code" framing in the issue's "Rough scope: Medium" note, but it's what's actually needed for every one of the four enum values to behave as described, in every place the issue's own text points to.

Separately, worth flagging but **not** in this issue's scope: Flow A bypassing `requiresCancellationReason` entirely (found above) looks like a pre-existing bug independent of #11 — I'd suggest filing that separately rather than folding it in here.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 15:38:56Z)**_

I dug into the actual code to settle these rather than reason abstractly. Here's what I found for each.

## Ambiguity #2: Is `rescheduledBy` acceptable for host detection, or must it be session-verified `isUserOrganizer`?

I checked whether cancellation's own `isCancellationUserHost` is actually more rigorous than I assumed. It isn't:

```ts
// apps/web/app/api/cancel/route.ts:38,54
const session = await getServerSession(...);
...
const result = await handleCancelBooking({
  bookingData: safeBookingData,       // includes `cancelledBy`, taken straight from the client's request body
  userId: session?.user?.id || -1,
});

// packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:154
const isCancellationUserHost = bookingToDelete.userId === userId || bookingToDelete.user.email === cancelledBy;
```

`cancelledBy` is **not** re-derived from the session — it's whatever email string the client puts in the POST body (sourced client-side from a prop that *happened* to come from the session at page-render time, but nothing stops a direct API call from sending an arbitrary value). So cancellation's own host-detection is already an OR of one verified signal (`userId` from session) and one **self-reported, spoofable** signal (`cancelledBy` email) — structurally identical to what `rescheduledBy` would be for reschedule.

This changes my earlier recommendation. Strictly mirroring cancellation means Flow B/C's host check should be the same shape: `isUserOrganizer || organizerUser.email === rescheduledBy` — not the stricter, session-only version I originally proposed. Using only `isUserOrganizer` would make reschedule *more* secure than cancellation already is, which is a legitimate choice but isn't "mirroring" — it's tightening.

Practically, this is low-severity either way: the only thing a spoofed identity buys someone is skipping a required-reason prompt, not access to data or an unauthorized action.

## Ambiguity #3: How much client-side UX parity does Flow B/C need?

Two real architectural facts, not a matter of preference:

1. `notes`'s `additionalNotesRequired` flag already gets "can't submit without it" behavior **for free**, with no bespoke UI code — because it's baked into the same `bookingFields` array that both the client (for rendering/inline validation) and server (for the final zod check) read. If `rescheduleReason.required` were computed the same static way, it'd get the same free behavior.
2. But `rescheduleReason`'s required-ness can't be static — it depends on who's submitting, and only `RegularBookingService.handler` (server-side, at submission time) reliably knows that. The client-facing event/bookingFields payload (`getPublicEvent.ts`) is visitor-agnostic (it's the same response for everyone who loads that event's booking page) and has no per-visitor "is this you, the host" concept today.

So there are two real options, not one obvious answer:
- **Server-only enforcement**: the field always renders as "optional" client-side (no asterisk, no proactive block), and a host/attendee who leaves it blank only finds out after clicking Submit, via a server-thrown error. This *does* satisfy the issue's literal text ("validation... that rejects an empty reason, shaped like the check at `handleCancelBooking.ts:161-166`" — which is itself just a server-side throw, not a proactive UI block).
- **Full parity with Cancel's proactive block**: requires adding a genuinely new "is the current visitor the host" signal to the Booker/booking-form (e.g. comparing `useSession()` against the event owner client-side), which doesn't exist anywhere in that component tree today. This is real net-new plumbing, not a copy of an existing pattern — unlike Flow A, where the button-disable is cheap since `isHost` is already always `true`.

## Ambiguity #4: Is there really a `$RCH$`-prefix inconsistency?

Confirmed, and it's more nuanced than "one line is missing a prefix":

- `packages/features/bookings/lib/BookingEmailSmsHandler.ts:126,153` (used by `RegularBookingService.ts:578` for **both** regular and round-robin reschedule notification emails — i.e., this covers Flow C) correctly builds `` cancellationReason: `$RCH$${rescheduleReason}` `` for the email payload. Emails are fine.
- `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/createBooking.ts:236` persists the **unprefixed** raw reason directly onto the new booking's DB `cancellationReason` column for non-seated Flow C reschedules. I checked the one consumer of that DB field I previously flagged (`apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-single-view.tsx:568-574`) — its label choice (`isCancelled ? "reason" : "reschedule_reason"`) doesn't actually sniff the `$RCH$` prefix at all, it uses a separate `reschedule` flag, and it renders the string **raw**, with no `$RCH$`-stripping.
- That means: for **seated** reschedules, where `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/reschedule/owner/*.ts` *does* persist the `$RCH$`-prefixed string to the DB, this same booking-detail view would render the literal text `$RCH$<reason>` to the user — a real, pre-existing display bug, independent of Issue #11, not something this issue's change would introduce, but also not obviously in scope for it either.

Given plan-mode constraints, I'll hold off updating the plan file until you weigh in on #2 and #3 — #4 is a factual finding rather than a decision, so let me know if you want it folded into this issue's scope or left as a separately-filed bug.
